items.name: Readability
items.evidence: The diff body wasn't captured. filter.py is a short 1086-byte bs4 script that, per the summary, mirrors the reference (decompose script/frames, strip on* attrs, replace 'javascript:'). It reads easily, but the policy lists are inline, not in named constants, and comments are sparse.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: One small remove_js function plus a main guard. The deny policy is inline literals, not named constants, and there is no URL-normalisation helper. It ends with chained str.replace calls ('javascript:', '<script'), which the conventions say to avoid.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: It checks argc and prints usage. It reads and writes without an explicit encoding, has no handling for a missing or unreadable file, and the scheme stripping is a literal case-sensitive replace with no normalisation. Nothing is silently swallowed.

items.name: Obfuscated vectors neutralised
items.evidence: It relies on literal str.replace('javascript:') and '<script'. 'JavaScript:', entity-encoded or tab-split schemes, and vbscript:/data:text/html all get through. It has no handling for <base>, <meta refresh>, srcdoc, formaction or svg/math href; only the on* check is case-insensitive, thanks to the bs4 parser.

items.name: Minimal edits on dirty documents
items.name_zh: 含恶意内容的文档仅做最小修改
items.evidence: It removes only the dangerous tags and on* attributes, but re-serialises the whole document with str(soup), which normalises quotes and void tags. The global 'javascript:' replace also changes benign text content.
